name: Com tam
summary: Cơm tấm is broken rice with grilled pork, the Saigon plate kept when the broken grains were not sold. Pour sweet fish sauce over the hot rice: one plate is honey-glazed pork chops, a fried egg, spring onions, and pickled papaya; another is marinated ribs with an omelet, egg rolls, and sausages; a third is cucumber, pickles, pork skin, and pork patties under a candy-like fish sauce.
origin: Farmers kept the broken grains because they were not sold. Cơm tấm is the essential Saigon plate, found on nearly every street.
history: Cơm tấm began here as broken rice that farmers kept because the grains were not sold.
culture: It is the go-to breakfast, and people also eat it at any meal. The smell of barbecued pork is on the street at all hours: breakfast, lunch, dinner, or supper.
texture: The ribs are grilled over low heat so the meat stays juicy and tender.
taste: Pour a generous amount of sweet fish sauce over the plate. That sweetness is the sauce.
howToEat: One plate is honey-glazed barbecued pork chops, a sunny-side-up egg, spring onions, and pickled papaya, with sweet fish sauce poured over the rice.
Another plate is marinated pork ribs on broken rice, with an omelet, egg rolls, and sausages, onion fat or pork grease, and fresh and pickled vegetables.

A third plate is a little dry, small-grain rice, cucumber, pickles, grilled ribs, pork skin, and pork patties. The fish sauce is candy-like: soak the hot rice in the sauce and eat it with the toppings.
where: All over the center. Use the nearest room, and Cơm tấm Ba Ghiền at 84 Đặng Văn Ngữ, Phú Nhuận, is one clue. Grilled pork noodle bowls sit on afternoon sidewalks next to cơm tấm.
seoTitle: Cơm tấm in Ho Chi Minh City
seoDescription: Three plates of cơm tấm in Ho Chi Minh City: honey-glazed pork with egg, ribs with omelet and egg rolls, and pork skin under a candy-like fish sauce.
